aboutH2: Westminster House: Addiction Recovery for Women and Youth Girls in New Westminster, BC
intro: Westminster House Society is a trauma-informed, gender-specific addiction recovery program that has been serving women and youth girls since 1981. The program utilizes the biopsychosocial model and complemented by cognitive behavioural therapy, introspective writing, and motivational interviewing to provide a broad range of services to the clients. The treatment services are delivered residentially, and women from Western Canada and beyond can access the services.

pillars.title: Addiction Recovery Services
pillars.body: The society offers addiction recovery services for youth girls, adult women, and their families. Westminster House is a non-profit charity organization that employs the best-cost strategy to provide upscale, multidisciplinary, and community-based services to provide a high value of service at an affordable price. The program has both private and publicly funded options available. Through Facebook, interested parties can learn more and see the successes.

pillars.title: Addiction-Free Environment
pillars.body: Westminster House is an addiction-free environment and supports women to permanently stop using substances, including nicotine, alcohol, and prescription and illicit drugs and process addictions. The program is regarded as one of Vancouver’s best drug rehab centres due to their approach to helping women overcome their addictions with the use of holistic treatment.

pillars.title: Building Resilience
pillars.body: At Westminster House, the goal is not only to facilitate addiction recovery but also to help women build resilience so that they may overcome the effects of trauma and addiction and reclaim their lives in their treatment centre in Vancouver. The approach adopted by Westminster House is effective as evidenced by the success stories that many women who have graduated have shared.

overview: Westminster House is a residential drug rehab center offering evidence-based practices and holistic therapies to female adults who are recovering from addiction. The center has been providing a safe and supportive environment for women for over three decades and is one of the few residential recovery centers in British Columbia. With its personalized “holistic” recovery model and principles from the 12-step approach, Westminster House is dedicated to empowering women to take responsibility for their ongoing recovery process.

afterOverview: The center’s recovery program provides clients with the necessary tools to overcome addiction and trust their own ability to reclaim a drug-free existence. Westminster House strongly encourages family members to participate in educational meetings, self-help programs, and other therapeutic activities to enhance healing and promote lasting recovery. The center offers amenities such as 12 step programs, substance abuse treatment, residential drug rehab, and a variety of therapies including holistic, evidence-based practices, yoga, meditation, and art & nature therapy. The highly qualified staff is committed to supporting clients in their journey towards a fulfilling and healthy lifestyle.

location.heading: Westminster House in New Westminster, British Columbia
location.intro: Westminster House is on Seventh Street in New Westminster, the small Metro Vancouver city on the Fraser River, with its recovery homes a short walk from one another. Downtown Vancouver is about 30 minutes away by car or SkyTrain, Burnaby and Surrey are 15 to 20 minutes, Coquitlam is about 20 minutes, Abbotsford in the Fraser Valley is under an hour, and Victoria is about 3.5 hours with the Tsawwassen ferry.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Westminster House cost?
faqs.a: recovery.com lists an estimated private-pay rate of about $9,000 a month for the 90-day program; the centre's own site does not publish fees. Fraser Health funded places are also available through a referral package, and you need funding in place before admission. Aftercare is free for alumnae.
The adult primary program is 90 days, and the full continuum of care can run up to six months. The youth and emerging adult program is six months, and the Aftercare Program is free for every alumna.

faqs.q: Is the program only for women?
faqs.a: Yes, it is a gender-specific program for women and youth girls only.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for the youth girl program?
faqs.a: The youth girl program is for girls aged 14-24 years.

faqs.q: Do I need to detox before coming to Westminster House?
faqs.a: No, you do not have to be abstinent before intake, according to the centre's admissions page. Westminster House lists medically supervised detox and stabilization among its services. Tell the intake team what you use and how much so they can plan a safe start.

faqs.q: Where is Westminster House and how do I get there?
faqs.a: Westminster House is at 228 Seventh Street in New Westminster, in Metro Vancouver. It is about 30 minutes from downtown Vancouver by car or SkyTrain and 15 to 20 minutes from Burnaby and Surrey. Bring no more than one suitcase, and leave phones and laptops at home if you can.

Many residents move into Westminster House's substance-free recovery housing, which can last up to a year. The Aftercare Program is free for every alumna, whenever she graduated, and includes weekly relapse prevention groups, one-to-one counselling, help with work, school and housing, and meals.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to access the program?
faqs.a: The program has both private and publicly funded options available. The cost varies depending on the program chosen.

faqs.q: Can I access the program virtually?
faqs.a: The treatment program is delivered residentially. The family support group meets online on Wednesday evenings.
Yes, Westminster House Society is licensed and accredited by CARF Canada.

faqs.q: How can I apply for the program?
faqs.a: You can apply for the program by contacting Westminster House Society through their website or phone.
